data.name: Demon Hunter 2: New Chapter
data.detailed_description:
Twenty years ago, in a frightening battle Dawn Harlock stopped the Archdemon Ragnar from descending upon the world. Turns out this was not the end of all the grim mysteries and adventures.

PLAY THE SEQUEL OF THE CAPTIVATING ""DEMON HUNTER: CHRONICLES FROM BEYOND"" HIDDEN OBJECT GAME!
Dawn’s foster father professor Ashmore died when trying to prevent the demon from breaking into this world. She realized than that she is the last remaining member of the mysterious ancient order of demon hunters and the last one standing in the fight against evil threatening to unravel this world.

TRAVEL THROUGH 31 HAND PAINTED LOCATIONS FULL OF PUZZLES AND SECRETS!
Her biggest concern was always to prepare for Ragnar’s return as it was already foretold. But Dawn kept herself busy as a detective, solving paranormal cases around the world and visiting mysterious places where the dark forces are hiding.

A CAPTIVATING STORY PACKED WITH MYSTERIES AND RIDDLES!
One day she receives a call from a mysterious doctor Stuart Williams, who claims to be Dawns foster father’s long-time friend. He promises valuable information about Dawns biological parents that may shed some light on her eerie past shrouded in mystery.

NEW MINI GAMES AND NOT-SO-EASY HO SCENES!
Dawns put on her detective hat to investigate the information that threatens to shake the core of her very existence. She will embark on a mystery adventure that will change everything forever.

Features

  • Play the sequel of the captivating "Demon Hunter: Chronicles from Beyond" hidden object game!
  • Travel through 31 hand painted locations full of puzzles and secrets!
  • A captivating story packed with mysteries and riddles!
  • New mini games and not-so-easy ho scenes!
  • Immersive gameplay with plenty of hidden objects!

reviews.review:
Had a fun time with this one. I always enjoy when a series has not only a direct sequel that is related to the previous game's story but also one with the same protagonist. So, with that I guess I will talk about the story first. The game continues the story from the first but after a time. The gameplay is mostly the same, except this time the amulet is now a more prominent part of the game and featured in your inventory as you play.

Whereas the first game had you exploring a single location, this game now expands to cover more areas. It's broken up to mostly be you arriving somewhere with a handful of scenes you unlock and explore before leaving and then being given another batch. I kind of don't have strong opinions either way about this, I do like exploring a large map all at once and it makes the locations seem more authentic, but even when every location remains accessible the game tends to have you clearing areas so there is no need to go back to them later. Or, if there is a reason to go back, it's something from very early game that you had forgotten about.

The art style is still very I guess "classic-looking?" The first game has this vibe of the 1930s, the year it takes place in, and this is 20 years later, so has a 50s vibe which still leaves both of them feeling very retro. The voice acting is also still kind of cheesy, but I love it and the style nor voice acting bothered me.

The puzzles and hidden object scenes are very standard, nothing really stood out to me as being either particularly innovative or challenging. But that's fine, and a lot of times these games are more "comfort food" for me than looking to test my skills, though I welcome more difficult puzzles if the game has them.

This game doesn't have a bonus adventure either, like the first game, but like the first game as well, this one has collectibles for you to find too if you want to achievement hunt. There is no difficulty requirement either for the achievements so you can also play it on a lower difficulty if you want to be able to check the map for locations with action and be able to see the visual hints for hidden object scenes as well. I found the most challenging achievement to be finishing a hidden object scene in 60 seconds or less, but I was still able to complete that before finishing the game so I didn't have to start a new game and try again.

This goes does not have any difficulty-related achievements.
This game does have collectibles.
This game does not have a bonus adventure.
I did not have any technical issues with this game.
